title: Coin Change
statement: You have coins of several values and as many of each as you like. Given a target amount, find the fewest coins that add up to exactly that amount. If no mix of coins can make it, return -1. Making amount 0 takes 0 coins.

example.caption: With coins 1, 2 and 5, amount 11 is 5 + 5 + 1, which is 3 coins.

output.label: dp[a] = fewest coins to make a

idea.sentence: dp[a] is the fewest coins that make amount a. Try each coin as the last one, so dp[a] = 1 + the smallest dp[a - coin] over the coins that fit.

jargon.plain: Fill a table of small answers from the smallest case up, each cell built from cells already filled.
A stand-in value for "not possible". Here it is infinity, so a real count always beats it in a min.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: the coin list, then the amount, e.g. [1,2,5], 11

compare.optimalLabel: One table cell per amount, one lookup per coin
compare.unit: coin choices tried (rough; brute is exponential, 2n is the closest curve)

rows.name: Brute force recursion
rows.note: Tries every coin at every step and solves the same leftover amount many times.

rows.name: dp table (bottom-up)
rows.note: Each of the n + 1 cells tries up to k coins and reads one earlier cell per coin.

fast.takeaway: The leftover after the last coin is a smaller amount you already solved, so each cell is just a min over a few earlier cells.

stages.title: Table of infinity
stages.note: dp[0] = 0. Every other amount starts as infinity, meaning no way found yet.

stages.title: Try each coin last
stages.note: For amount a, each coin c that fits offers dp[a - c] + 1. Keep the smallest.

stages.title: Answer or -1
stages.note: dp[amount] is the answer. If it is still infinity, return -1.

edges.title: Amount zero
edges.why: dp[0] = 0 is the base case. The loop never runs and the answer is already there.

edges.title: Coin bigger than the amount
edges.why: No coin fits, so dp[3] stays infinity. The c <= a check also keeps the index a - c from going negative.

edges.title: Greedy takes too many
edges.why: Taking the biggest coin first gives 4 + 1 + 1 = 3 coins. The table tries every last coin and finds 3 + 3.

edges.title: No exact mix
edges.why: Every coin fits but no sum lands on 11. Cells reading an infinity stay infinity.

gotchas.text: The table needs amount + 1 cells so that index amount exists. Cell 0 is the base case and the only one that starts at 0.
Skip a coin when c > a. Otherwise a - c is negative and reads outside the table.

Infinity + 1 is still Infinity, so unreachable cells stay unreachable inside Math.min. Check for Infinity at the end and return -1. Infinity also cannot be sent through JSON, so the panels show the string "inf".
Do not use math.MaxInt as the sentinel. dp[a-c]+1 then overflows to the most negative number and wins every min. Use amount + 1: no real answer needs that many coins, and adding 1 is safe.
Go has a built-in min since 1.21. On older versions, write a small helper. The signature differs from math.Min, which takes floats.

recap.pattern: 1-D DP: min over the last choice
recap.key: dp[a] = 1 + min(dp[a - c]) over coins c <= a, with dp[0] = 0 and infinity for unreachable amounts.
moves: dp[0] = 0, every other cell is infinity
For each amount a from 1 up
Try each coin c <= a: dp[a] = min(dp[a], dp[a - c] + 1)
Answer is dp[amount], or -1 if it is still infinity
